What_It_Shows: In the Aug. 15, 2017 Trump Tower transcript Trump says 'very fine people, on both sides' while expressly excluding 'neo-Nazis and the White nationalists' who 'should be condemned totally.'

The Aug. 14, 2017 White House statement has Trump condemning 'the KKK, neo-Nazis, white supremacists, and other hate groups' as 'criminals and thugs,' contradicting Biden's claim he never condemned them.

Mueller Report Vol. II recounts Cohen's false congressional statements and a 'party line' via the President's personal counsel; it does not establish that Trump personally directed Cohen to lie to Congress as BuzzFeed claimed.
The April 23, 2020 White House briefing transcript shows Trump asking whether disinfectant could be used 'by injection' or 'almost a cleaning,' not telling Americans to drink bleach.

The May 16, 2018 White House sanctuary-state roundtable transcript shows Trump saying 'These aren't people. These are animals' in the context of discussing MS-13 gang members, not undocumented immigrants generally.

DOI OIG's Lafayette Park special review finds USPP cleared the park to install antiscale fencing after officer injuries and property damage, and evidence did not support clearing it so Trump could walk to St. John's Church.

The House Judiciary/Weaponization interim staff report documents the FBI already possessed Hunter Biden's laptop and that DOJ later authenticated it in court, undercutting the 'classic earmarks of Russian disinfo' framing of the NY Post story.
The full Aug. 15, 2017 transcript supplies the condemnation sentence memes omit: Trump excludes neo-Nazis and white nationalists from 'very fine people' and says they 'should be condemned totally.'
Same April 23, 2020 official briefing transcript is the primary record of the disinfectant remarks later recycled as 'drink/inject bleach' characterizations.
DOI OIG finds USPP did not authorize CS tear gas for the June 1, 2020 clearing and that officers used pepper balls/smoke; it also rejects the claim clearing was solely for Trump's church photo-op.
The March 16, 2024 Ohio rally transcript places the 'bloodbath' line in a discussion of auto imports/China-Mexico manufacturing, not a call for political violence.
The Dec. 5, 2023 Hannity town-hall transcript shows Trump saying 'Except for day one' about being a dictator, then specifying closing the border and drilling, and 'After that, I'm not a dictator.'

Mueller's July 24, 2019 House Judiciary testimony (official hearing record) states DOJ policy and fairness led him not to make a traditional prosecution decision on the President—not that he would have indicted but for OLC policy as Nadler framed it.

In the Dec. 5, 2023 Hannity town hall Trump says you don't have to touch Social Security and criticizes opponents for wanting to raise the eligibility age—contradicting absolute claims he plans to cut Social Security benefits.
Same Hannity town-hall transcript pairs Trump's Social Security no-cut framing with energy-revenue arguments rather than a plan to cut Medicare benefits for seniors.

OMB's FY2020 Major Savings and Reforms Medicare chapters describe proposed savings via provider-payment reforms, GME/uncompensated-care reclassification, and fraud/waste measures, while stating the aim of protecting Medicare for seniors—not a benefit-slash package.
Trump's April 8, 2024 Truth Social video transcript says 'the states will determine' abortion law after Roe and does not call for a nationwide abortion ban.
Trump's July 5, 2024 Truth Social post states 'I know nothing about Project 2025' and 'I have nothing to do with them,' contradicting framing that Project 2025 is Trump's official plan.
The Ohio rally transcript's auto-industry 'bloodbath' context undercuts captions linking the clip to a desire for another January 6.
The Feb. 28, 2020 North Charleston rally transcript shows Trump calling Democrats' politicization of coronavirus 'their new hoax,' not labeling the disease itself a hoax.
The June 16, 2015 campaign-announcement transcript has Trump saying Mexico is 'sending' people who include 'rapists' and 'some, I assume, are good people,' not that 'all Mexicans are rapists.'
The Jan. 6, 2017 ODNI ICA states the assessment was drafted/coordinated among CIA, FBI, and NSA—three agencies—not all 17 U.S. intelligence organizations.

Mueller Report Vol. I states the investigation 'did not establish that members of the Trump Campaign conspired or coordinated with the Russian government,' undercutting absolute 'undeniable collusion' framing.

U.S. Capitol Police's release of the D.C. medical examiner finding states Officer Brian Sicknick died of natural causes (acute brainstem and cerebellar infarcts), not from being struck with a fire extinguisher.

The Aug. 12, 2020 press-conference transcript shows Trump saying he would terminate the payroll tax and protect Social Security via the general fund—not that he would terminate Social Security itself.

Trump's April 8, 2024 Truth Social video says he strongly supports IVF availability in every state, contradicting a blanket claim that Project 2025/Trump allies' plan restricts IVF and contraception as his plan.

Same Aug. 12, 2020 transcript has Trump pledging Social Security 'will be totally protected' while discussing terminating the payroll tax, contradicting claims he promised to gut Social Security and Medicare.

The Aug. 8, 2020 presidential memorandum in the Federal Register only directed Treasury to defer certain employee payroll-tax withholdings for Sept.–Dec. 2020—not an executive action cutting Social Security Trust Fund benefit payments.
The White House's own May 13, 2022 correction tweet states it 'previously misstated that vaccines were unavailable in January 2021' and should have said they were 'not widely available.'

FY2020 Major Savings and Reforms frames Medicare proposals as waste/fraud/provider-payment reforms while stating protection of Medicare for seniors—not annual cuts to Social Security/Medicare benefits for retirees.
Official FY2020 budget savings document describes Medicare integrity/provider reforms rather than cutting seniors' Social Security or Medicare benefit checks.

Trump v. United States (July 1, 2024) holds absolute immunity only for conclusive/preclusive constitutional acts, presumptive immunity for other official acts, and no immunity for unofficial acts—not blanket absolute criminal immunity.

The Feb. 10, 2024 Conway, SC rally transcript shows the 'whatever the hell they want' line conditioned on a NATO ally being 'delinquent' on bills—not an unconditioned invitation for Russia to invade any NATO ally.

JCT's JCX-67-17 revenue score of TCJA lists individual rate-bracket and standard-deduction changes applying across the rate schedule—not a corporate-only cut that left ordinary taxpayers with nothing.
The Dec. 26, 2018 Federal Register ATF final rule classifies bump-stock-type devices as machineguns and sets an effective date of March 26, 2019, documenting that bump stocks were banned.
The Nov. 10, 2015 Milwaukee GOP debate transcript shows Trump saying 'wages too high' in answering whether to raise the minimum wage to $15—not a claim that all American wages are too high.
Same JCT conference score documents broad individual-rate and standard-deduction provisions, undercutting claims that tax relief excluded the middle class entirely.

BLS CPS unemployment-rate series shows the COVID spike and recovery path; it does not support characterizing the January 2021 handoff as the worst unemployment since the Great Depression without that pandemic context.

DOL's Sept. 27, 2019 FLSA overtime final rule raised the standard salary threshold to $684/week ($35,568/year) effective Jan. 1, 2020—expanding overtime eligibility versus prior law, not cutting overtime benefits.

BEA international trade data is the official series for U.S. goods-and-services deficits, against which claims that Trump left 'one of the highest' deficits in history can be checked against later larger totals.
Same April 8, 2024 video transcript shows Trump's 2024 position as state-by-state determination with rape/incest/life exceptions, not a promise to ban abortion nationwide regardless of Congress.

Primary budget text shows proposed Medicare savings via payment/fraud reforms and a stated aim to protect Medicare, contradicting absolute 'slash Medicare benefits' characterizations of those budgets.
